extraction_notes: Built by enumerating every U.S. president from #1 (Washington) through presidency #47 (Trump's second term) on the cited Wikipedia 'List of presidents of the United States by home state' page, mapping each individual to their birth state, then aggregating COUNT(DISTINCT president) GROUP BY birth_state. Non-consecutive presidencies (Cleveland 22 and 24; Trump 45 and 47) were collapsed to one person each so they contribute one count, not two. Andrew Jackson's birth state is recorded as South Carolina, matching Wikipedia's primary attribution; the historical NC/SC dispute is documented in curation.json rather than reflected in the CSV. No rows were added from any source other than the cited Wikipedia list, and no states with zero presidents born there are included (HAVING COUNT >= 1).
temporal_note_at_registration: Snapshot taken 2026-04-27 from Wikipedia 'List of presidents of the United States by home state'. Covers presidencies 1 through 47 (George Washington through Donald Trump's second term, inaugurated January 2025). Cleveland (22 and 24) and Trump (45 and 47) each count as one person, so the table aggregates over 45 distinct individuals. The row set will grow only when a new individual is inaugurated as U.S. president whose birth state is not already represented; existing per-state counts may also increment over time.

curation_record.collection_summary: Aggregation instance counting U.S. presidents per birth state. The implicit source table is the closed, well-defined set of all 45 distinct individuals who have served as U.S. president (presidencies 1-47, with Cleveland and Trump each counted once). Wikipedia's 'List of presidents of the United States by home state' enumerates this set and gives a birth state for every president, so the aggregation is exhaustive over the universe at the snapshot date (2026-04-27).
curation_record.source_coverage_notes: Single Wikipedia source covers all 45 distinct presidents. 21 distinct birth states appear; the CSV lists every state that has produced at least one president and excludes states with zero (HAVING COUNT >= 1) by definition of the aggregation. Per-state breakdown derived from the source: Virginia 8 (Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, W.H. Harrison, Tyler, Z. Taylor, Wilson), Ohio 7 (Grant, Hayes, Garfield, B. Harrison, McKinley, Taft, Harding), New York 5 (Van Buren, Fillmore, T. Roosevelt, F.D. Roosevelt, Trump), Massachusetts 4 (J. Adams, J.Q. Adams, Kennedy, G.H.W. Bush), North Carolina 2 (Polk, A. Johnson), Pennsylvania 2 (Buchanan, Biden), Texas 2 (Eisenhower, L.B. Johnson), Vermont 2 (Arthur, Coolidge), and one each for Arkansas (Clinton), California (Nixon), Connecticut (G.W. Bush), Georgia (Carter), Hawaii (Obama), Illinois (Reagan), Iowa (Hoover), Kentucky (Lincoln), Missouri (Truman), Nebraska (Ford), New Hampshire (Pierce), New Jersey (Cleveland), South Carolina (Jackson), totaling 45 distinct presidents. The aggregate row total (sum of counts) equals 45, which matches the count of distinct individuals.
curation_record.decision_log: 1) Used Wikipedia's 'List of presidents of the United States by home state' as the single authoritative list; this page enumerates every president and their birth state, so a single source is sufficient for an exhaustive aggregation. 2) Defined the COUNT semantics as COUNT(DISTINCT president), so Cleveland (presidencies 22 and 24) and Trump (presidencies 45 and 47) each contribute one count to their birth state rather than two; this matches the natural-language intent of 'how many presidents were born here' and avoids inflating New York and New Jersey. 3) Coded Andrew Jackson's birth state as 'South Carolina' to match Wikipedia's primary attribution, even though North Carolina has historically also claimed him; if a future audit prefers North Carolina, the SC row would drop to 0 (excluded under HAVING COUNT >= 1) and NC would rise to 3. 4) Sorted rows alphabetically by Birth State for a stable default order rather than count-descending, which would have leaned toward top_k semantics. 5) Kept the schema deliberately narrow (key + numeric) to make the aggregation crisp; deferred a possible 'Presidents Born There' string-aggregated names column to keep the instance from drifting toward multi_attribute_projection.
curation_record.normalization_decisions: Birth State values use the full English state name as 'key' type (e.g., 'South Carolina', not 'S.C.' or 'SC'), consistent with the column-type convention in curation_protocol.md Section 6. 'Presidents Born' is a bare integer with no thousands separator. Non-consecutive presidencies are collapsed to one person each before aggregation; this is a curation decision and is documented above. Andrew Jackson is normalized to a single state ('South Carolina') rather than emitted with a boundary-aware label like 'North Carolina; South Carolina' because the source presents one primary attribution; the dispute is recorded under open_questions instead of changing the schema.
curation_record.open_questions: 1) Andrew Jackson's birth state is historically disputed between South Carolina and North Carolina (the Waxhaws region straddles the border). The instance follows Wikipedia's primary attribution to SC, but a stricter source (e.g., Library of Congress or Tennessee historical society treatments) might warrant either reassigning to NC or representing him with a multi-state label. Either alternative changes the SC, NC, or schema rows. 2) The set will grow each time a new individual is inaugurated whose birth state is not already represented, and existing per-state counts may also increment; the table is therefore a 2026-04-27 snapshot, not a permanent ground truth. 3) An optional 'Presidents Born There' STRING_AGG-style column listing the names per state would aid verification but would shift the instance toward multi_attribute_projection; left out for now to keep the aggregation pure.
